messages:
ryan: Hi team, fresh hire here. Pulled the repo and ran `docker-compose up` but Postgres immediately exits with `FATAL: database files are incompatible with server`. I'm on mac + Docker Desktop. Any idea what's gone wrong?

emily: Welcome! That message usually means the data directory was initialized by a different PG major version (e.g., data created by PG 12 but current image is PG 14). Did you reuse an existing named volume?

ryan: I didn't think so, but compose uses a named volume `redwood_pgdata`. I cloned the repo and ran compose, so maybe I have leftovers from an older project. The container logs show: `FATAL: database files are incompatible with server` and earlier `PG_VERSION: 12` in the volume files.

josh: Yep that's exactly it. Two options: 1) if you don't need the old data, remove the volume and let postgres init a fresh DB; or 2) bring up a container with the older PG version to access/upgrade the data (or run pg_upgrade).

priya: Commands to inspect first, so you don't delete anything accidentally:```bash
docker volume ls | grep redwood_pgdata
docker run --rm -v redwood_pgdata:/data alpine sh -c "ls -la /data && cat /data/PG_VERSION"
```That will show what's inside and the PG_VERSION file.

ryan: Ran that and it printed `12`. I remember my laptop had a side project using Postgres 12 earlier. So the volume is from that.

emily: If you're ok losing local data (most dev setups are ephemeral), easiest: `docker-compose down -v` in the repo to remove containers and named volumes, or `docker volume rm redwood_pgdata`. Then `docker-compose up` will create a fresh cluster under the current image.

josh: If you need to preserve old DB contents, do this instead: start a postgres:12 container mounting the same volume so the older server can read it, dump the DB (pg_dumpall or pg_dump), then import into the new postgres:14 image or run pg_upgrade. Example:```bash
docker run --rm -d --name pg12 -v redwood_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pass postgres:12
# then pg_dump from host or run psql/dump inside a client container
```

priya: Another tip: pin the postgres image in docker-compose.yml to the major version we expect (e.g., `image: postgres:14`) so new developers don't accidentally spin a different major version. Also add a README note about `docker-compose down -v` and the implication.

ryan: Removed the old volume (I wasn't using any data) and `docker-compose up` booted cleanly. Thanks all! Learned an expensive-sounding lesson about named volumes. :grimacing: 

emily: Yay! If you want a non-destructive way next time, you can rename the volume before deleting: `docker volume create --name redwood_pgdata_backup && docker run --rm -v redwood_pgdata:/from -v redwood_pgdata_backup:/to alpine ash -c "cd /from && cp -a . /to"` — then you have a copy.

infra-bot: Dev onboarding doc updated with a troubleshooting section for PG major-version mismatches + recommended `docker-compose down -v` note: https://redwood-inference.internal/docs/dev-setup#pg-version-mismatch (cc @new-hires) :book:
